{"text": "The function `format` formats Python and documentation files in a project.", "type": "intent"},
{"text": "The function `format` determines which files have been modified since the last commit using the `tools.modified_files()` method.", "type": "structural"},
{"text": "The function `format` sets a flag to format all files instead of just the modified ones if the `requirements/tools.txt` file has changed.", "type": "behavioural"},
{"text": "The function `format` filters the files into a list of Python source files and a list of documentation files (`.rst`, `.md`).", "type": "dataflow"},
{"text": "The function `format` returns early if no files need formatting.", "type": "behavioural"},
{"text": "For each Python file, the function `format` reads its contents line by line and removes redundant `# pragma: no cover` comments matching patterns defined in the project's `.coveragerc` configuration file.", "type": "dataflow"},
{"text": "The function `format` writes the cleaned-up source back to each Python file, preserving the shebang line and adding a header if necessary.", "type": "behavioural"},
{"text": "The function `format` runs `codespell` to correct spelling mistakes.", "type": "structural"},
{"text": "The function `format` runs `ruff` to fix style issues.", "type": "structural"},
{"text": "The function `format` runs `shed` to ensure compatibility with Python 3.9+.", "type": "structural"},
{"text": "The function `format` relies on the helper functions `should_format_file`, `should_format_doc_file`, and `pip_tool` to perform specific tasks.", "type": "structural"},
{"text": "If no files are found that need formatting, the function `format` exits without making any changes or raising exceptions.", "type": "behavioural"}
]
